column7: LocalStorage.UpdateSecret was a bare GORM Save of a struct the caller read earlier and unlocked, and it was the SHARED primitive for eight operations, so every one inherited its defects. Resurrection half: Save's 0-rows fallback upserts with deleted_at=NULL, so ANY of the eight landing after a concurrent DeleteSecret brought the secret back -- and DeleteSecret also revokes the secret's shares and ACLs, so it returned WITHOUT them, with no secret.restored audit event, without going through RestoreSecret, invisible to the restore UI and never reclaimed by the purge (which only takes deleted rows). Fixed by replacing the primitive with UpdateSecretFields, a per-field-pointer conditional UPDATE scoped to deleted_at IS NULL, with every caller naming only the columns it owns. Red on PRISTINE origin/main with only the test file added: the secret row was live again after a delete that reported success. Found by C-GUARD-3 guard 1
